title: Food Chains and Food Webs
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Food Chains and Food Webs Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Classify organisms as producers, consumers or decomposers; describe food chains and food webs in Ontario habitats and how a change to one population affects others. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Habitats and Communities)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on producers, consumers, decomposers, food chains and food webs, with Ontario forest and pond examples. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy flows from the Sun to plants to animals.
key_sub: Producers make food; consumers eat; decomposers break down dead things.
body_html:
How to think about it

A food chain shows who eats whom. The arrows point from the food to the eater.

  • Producers (plants and algae) make their own food using sunlight.
  • Consumers eat other living things: herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both.
  • Decomposers (fungi, bacteria, worms) break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil.
  • A food web is many linked food chains. If one population changes, others change too.
Example

Grass → hare → lynx. Which is the producer?

the grass makes its own food

Answer: grass

Example

If the hares disappear, what happens to the lynx?

lynx eat hares

less food

Answer: the lynx population falls

Common mistakes

  • Drawing the arrows backwards (the arrow points to the eater).
  • Thinking decomposers are not important.
  • Thinking a change to one animal affects only that animal.

faq.q: Why do food chains start with a plant?
faq.a: Plants are producers. They capture energy from the Sun and make food, so all the energy in the chain starts with them.

faq.q: What is the difference between a food chain and a food web?
faq.a: A food chain is one path of energy. A food web shows many food chains linked together.
They break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil so new plants can grow.

items.q: Which living things are consumers?
c: animals, because they eat other living things
items.e: Consumers cannot make their own food.

items.q: Food chain: pondweed → tadpole → water beetle → heron. Which is the producer?
items.e: The producer makes its own food using sunlight; it is always first.

items.q: Food chain: algae → mayfly larva → trout → otter. What does the trout eat in this chain?
items.e: The arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which is a scavenger that eats dead animals?
items.e: Scavengers clean up dead animals.

items.q: Food chain: phytoplankton → krill → whale. Which is the first consumer (it eats the producer)?
items.e: It eats the plant at the start of the chain.

items.q: Food chain: grass → rabbit → fox. What eats the rabbit in this chain?
items.e: The arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Is a bracket fungus a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Decomposers break down dead plants, animals and waste.

items.q: Food chain: grain → field vole → kestrel. Which is the top predator?
items.e: The top predator is at the end of the chain; nothing in the chain eats it.

items.q: Is a maple tree a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Producers make their own food from sunlight.

items.q: Forest food web: acorns are eaten by squirrels, chipmunks and deer. Foxes eat squirrels and chipmunks. Wolves eat deer. What does the fox eat?
items.e: Read the links to the fox.

items.q: Food chain: oak leaves → caterpillar → blue tit → sparrowhawk. Which is the producer?
items.e: The producer makes its own food using sunlight; it is always first.

items.q: Food chain: oak leaves → caterpillar → blue tit → sparrowhawk. What does the caterpillar eat in this chain?
items.e: The arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Is an earthworm a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Decomposers break down dead plants, animals and waste.

items.q: What is prey?
c: an animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal
items.e: Mice are prey for owls.

items.q: Food chain: seaweed → periwinkle → crab → herring gull. What does the crab eat in this chain?
items.e: The arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Why are decomposers important?
c: They break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil for plants.
items.e: Without them, dead matter would pile up.

items.q: Which animal is an omnivore?
c: a black bear (eats berries and fish)
items.e: Omnivores eat plants and animals.

items.q: Lake food chain: algae → zooplankton → minnow → walleye. What does the minnow eat?
items.e: Follow the arrow into the minnow.

items.q: Is mold on bread a producer, a consumer or a decomposer?
items.e: Decomposers break down dead plants, animals and waste.

items.q: What does an arrow in a food chain show?
c: the direction energy moves when one thing is eaten
items.e: The arrow points to the eater.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: heron, pondweed, tadpole, water beetle?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which word describes a living thing that eats only plants?
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: Use the pond food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: algae → mosquito larva → guppy → heron.

items.q: Bacteria in the soil break down a dead tree. What role do they play?
items.e: Bacteria recycle nutrients.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: aphid, blackbird, ladybug, nettles?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: crab, herring gull, periwinkle, seaweed?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Why are there usually fewer wolves than deer in a forest?
c: Energy is lost at each step, so there is less energy for animals higher up the chain.
items.e: Each level supports fewer animals.

items.q: Which animal in an Ontario forest is a carnivore?
items.e: Foxes hunt small animals.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: fox, grass, rabbit?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: In the same forest web, a disease kills most of the oak trees. Which animals lose food first?
items.e: Herbivores depend directly on the producer.

items.q: Use the meadow food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: grass → grasshopper → mouse → fox.

items.q: Meadow food chain: clover → grasshopper → garter snake → red-tailed hawk. Which is a carnivore that is also eaten?
items.e: The snake eats grasshoppers and is eaten by hawks.

items.q: This is an ocean food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: phytoplankton → krill → humpback whale.

items.q: In a food chain, what is a consumer?
c: a living thing that eats only plants
a living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things
a living thing that hunts and eats other animals
a living thing that eats only animals
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: In a food chain, what is a prey?
c: a living thing that hunts and eats other animals
a living thing that is hunted and eaten by other animals
a living thing that gets its energy by eating other living things
a living thing that eats only animals
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: Which food chain is in the correct order: krill, phytoplankton, whale?
items.e: Start with the producer; each arrow points to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Which word describes a living thing that makes its own food using energy from sunlight?
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: In a food chain, what is a predator?
c: a living thing that eats only animals
a living thing that eats only plants
a living thing that hunts and eats other animals
a living thing that makes its own food using energy from sunlight
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: In a food chain, what is a carnivore?
c: a living thing that eats only animals
a living thing that eats only plants
a living thing that hunts and eats other animals
a living thing that is hunted and eaten by other animals
items.e: Learn the food chain words.

items.q: Use the ocean food web. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the eater: phytoplankton → krill → humpback whale.

items.q: This is a pond food web. In this web, the heron's food is: frog, guppy. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only animals.

items.q: This is a pond food web. How many kinds of food does the heron eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the heron: frog, guppy.

items.q: This is an ocean food web. Which animal eats the herring?
items.e: An arrow goes from the herring to the humpback whale.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. Which animal eats the water lettuce?
items.e: An arrow goes from the water lettuce to the turtle.

items.q: This is an ocean food web. In this web, the humpback whale's food is: krill, herring. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only animals.

items.q: Look at the coral reef food web. Which animal eats the zooplankton?
items.e: An arrow goes from the zooplankton to the small fish.

items.q: This is a school garden food web. Which animal eats the garden lizard?
items.e: An arrow goes from the garden lizard to the snake.

items.q: In an Ontario forest: maple leaves → caterpillar → chickadee → hawk. Which is the producer?
items.e: Plants make their own food using sunlight.

items.q: A wolf eats deer. A deer eats grass. What is the deer?
items.e: Deer eat only plants.

items.q: This is an ocean food web. In this web, the orca's food is: seal, sea otter. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only animals.

items.q: Use the pond food web. Which animal eats the snail?
items.e: An arrow goes from the snail to the turtle.

items.q: Look at the meadow food web. What does the grasshopper eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the grass to the grasshopper, so the grasshopper eats grass.

items.q: This is a school garden food web. How many kinds of food does the spider eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the spider: grasshopper.

items.q: A farmer sprays a field to kill all the grasshoppers. What might happen to the frogs that eat them?
c: The frogs have less food and their number may fall.
items.e: Changes travel through food webs.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. In this web, the heron's food is: frog, guppy. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: It eats only animals.

items.q: Use the meadow food web. Which of these is food for the hawk?
items.e: The arrow goes from the mouse to the hawk, so the hawk eats a mouse.

items.q: What do decomposers return to the soil?
items.e: Nutrients help new plants grow.

items.q: This is a pond food web. What does the mosquito larva eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the algae to the mosquito larva, so the mosquito larva eats algae.

items.q: Use the coral reef food web. How many kinds of food does the squid eat in this web?
items.e: Count the arrows pointing to the squid: small fish.

items.q: Look at the pond food web. What does the dragonfly eat?
items.e: The arrow goes from the mosquito larva to the dragonfly, so the dragonfly eats a mosquito larva.

items.q: Look at the coral reef food web. A disease kills most of the small fish. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The squid eats only small fish. Without them, the squid has little food.

items.q: Food chain: grain → field vole → kestrel. If all the field voles were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be fewer grain.
There would probably be more grain.
items.e: With no field voles eating them, more grain survive.

items.q: This is a school garden food web. A disease kills most of the grasshoppers. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The spider eats only grasshoppers. Without them, the spider has little food.

items.q: Food chain: dandelion → snail → song thrush → cat. If all the snails were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be fewer dandelions.
There would probably be more dandelions.
items.e: With no snails eating them, more dandelions survive.

items.q: Look at the coral reef food web. Most of the sharks are removed from the coral reef. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the shark eats parrotfish. With fewer predators, more parrotfish survive.

items.q: Food chain: phytoplankton → krill → whale. If all the whales were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be fewer krill.
There would probably be more krill.
items.e: With no whales eating them, more krill survive.

items.q: Use the pond food web. Most of the herons are removed from the pond. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the heron eats small fish. With fewer predators, more small fish survive.

items.q: Food chain: dandelion → snail → song thrush → cat. If all the song thrushes were removed, what would most likely happen first?
c: There would probably be fewer snails.
There would probably be more snails.
items.e: With no song thrushes eating them, more snails survive.

items.q: This is a pond food web. Most of the frogs are removed from the pond. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the frog eats dragonflys. With fewer predators, more dragonflys survive.

items.q: Food chain: oak leaves → caterpillar → blue tit → sparrowhawk. If the number of oak leaves fell, what would most likely happen to the caterpillars?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: Food chain: oak leaves → caterpillar → blue tit → sparrowhawk. If the number of caterpillars fell, what would most likely happen to the blue tits?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: Snowshoe hares eat plants. Lynx eat hares. If the number of hares falls, what happens to the lynx?
c: Lynx start making their own food.
There is less food, so the number of lynx falls.
items.e: Predators depend on their prey.

items.q: This is a forest food web. A disease kills most of the deer. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The wolf eats only deer. Without them, the wolf has little food.

items.q: Lake food chain: algae → zooplankton → minnow → walleye → osprey. What eats the walleye?
items.e: The arrow from walleye points to the osprey.

items.q: This is a meadow food web. A disease kills most of the grasshoppers. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The frog eats only grasshoppers. Without them, the frog has little food.

items.q: Where does the energy in almost every food chain come from first?
items.e: Plants use the Sun's energy to make food.

items.q: Use the pond food web. A disease kills most of the algae. Which population would most likely go down first?
items.e: The mosquito larva eats only algae. Without them, the mosquito larva has little food.

items.q: Look at the meadow food web. Most of the hawks are removed from the meadow. Which population would most likely go up at first?
items.e: Only the hawk eats snakes. With fewer predators, more snakes survive.

items.q: What is a food web?
c: many food chains that are linked together
items.e: Most animals eat more than one thing.

items.q: Food chain: acorns → wood mouse → tawny owl. If the number of wood mice fell, what would most likely happen to the tawny owls?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: Every food chain starts with
items.e: Producers make the food that all the other organisms depend on.

items.q: What is a top predator?
c: an animal at the end of a food chain that nothing in the chain eats
the first living thing in a chain
items.e: Such as an owl or a fox.

items.q: A herbivore eats
items.e: Rabbits and deer are herbivores.

items.q: Pond food web: algae and duckweed are eaten by tadpoles and snails. Fish eat tadpoles. Herons eat fish and frogs. Which living things are producers?
items.e: Producers are the plants and algae.

items.q: Leah counted the animals in a school garden: 120 aphids, 15 ladybugs. Why are there more aphids than ladybugs?
c: Each ladybug eats many aphids, and less energy reaches the ladybugs.
items.e: Prey usually outnumber predators.

items.q: Which change would affect the most organisms in a food web?
items.e: Every food chain begins with producers, so all consumers depend on them.

items.q: In a pond: algae → tadpole → fish → heron. Which is the top consumer?
items.e: The heron is at the end of the chain.

items.q: Can an animal be both predator and prey?
c: Yes, for example a blue tit eats caterpillars but is eaten by sparrowhawks.
items.e: Middle of the chain.

items.q: What is a consumer?
c: an organism that gets energy by eating other organisms
a plant that makes its own food
items.e: Animals are consumers. They cannot make their own food.

items.q: Use the forest food web. The energy in the wolf's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the wolf.

items.q: A student drew a food chain: grasshopper → grass → mynah. What is wrong?
items.e: Correct: grass → grasshopper → mynah.

items.q: What does a food chain show?
c: what eats what, and how energy passes from one living thing to another
items.e: Arrows show energy flow.

items.q: This is a school garden food web. The energy in the ladybug's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the ladybug.

items.q: Why is a food web a better model of an ecosystem than one food chain?
c: Most animals eat more than one kind of food, and a web shows all the links.
items.e: One food chain leaves out many feeding links.

items.q: A carnivore eats
items.e: Hawks and wolves are carnivores.

items.q: Earthworms eat dead leaves. What role do they play?
items.e: Worms help recycle nutrients.

items.q: The number of mosquitoes in a pond fell after guppies were added. Why?
c: Guppies eat adult mosquitoes in the air.
items.e: Guppies are used to control mosquito breeding.

items.q: Look at the school garden food web. The energy in the snake's food first came from
items.e: Plants (producers) capture energy from sunlight. That energy passes along the food chain to the snake.

items.q: Why does a food chain always start with a plant (or other producer)?
c: Producers make their own food from sunlight.
items.e: Producers come first.

items.q: What is a producer?
c: a living thing that breaks down dead matter
an organism that makes its own food, like a plant
an animal that eats other animals
items.e: Producers, such as plants and algae, use sunlight to make their own food.
